knowledge_gaps: The design is sound as a controlled augmentation experiment, but it is not yet reproducible: the common epoch count, remaining budget, diagnostic time limit and validation-query cap are deferred. These require host accounting rather than web research.

Passing padding probes with both TF32 flags disabled establishes consistency only under those settings. The report must specify training and deployed predictor precision settings and verify predictor agreement under the actual host inference path.

Suffix supervision changes the expected weighting of positions and histories. Matching B/C controls this difference for C−B, but B−A also measures recency-dependent supervision weighting. Report retention probabilities and realized supervision counts rather than treating B−A as merely fewer targets.

The actual baseline objective, sampler and readout remain unavailable. Exact masking, candidate matching and preservation of connected prefix gradients therefore remain implementation requirements, not demonstrated capabilities. Code difficulty 5 is provisional; 6 is more defensible for the complete protocol.

The cited literature primarily supports diagnostics and evaluation cautions. Direct training-time sequence-cropping and recurrent augmentation precedents are needed to substantiate originality. Originality 4 and potential 7 are reasonable qualitative judgments, but no validation evidence establishes benefit.

No new architecture is necessary yet. Frozen-model deletion probes are a useful optional supplement, while deterministic truncation would be a separately budgeted control. Neither should silently expand the twelve-fit experiment. Retain the stated limits on intent attribution, sampled evaluation and single-seed conclusions.
